I don't care much for the backstory, but then I never did with Mortal Kombat, Tekken, Streetfighter... It's kind of fun playing some of the same characters in Seven Card Slugfest though!

Blue Haired Meerkat - Go for Devastation, the War Reprint is coming soon but will be smaller, and the Devastation box looks awesome. I half regret getting War when I did as I'd have been better off waiting. I'm waiting for a friend to visit his family in the states so I can cheekily ask him to pick up the Extended pack for Devastation that rebalances War for those who have it (in addition to extra goodies for Devastation) - the shipping and customs hit is just brutal for such a small item.

What surprised me is the depth of the game, it's subtle, but can be a real brain-burner. I read a blog where Brad Talton was talking about how the game emerged from his desire to create a game that used all mechanics, so each fighter has very different mechanisms for how they fight. Really must get more people to play it, though sadly the board game group in London have a "no 2 player game rule" which I might ask if I can bend by running a 4/6 player tournament since I have some spare boards that I can set up battles on

posts.name: Reckless
posts.cooked:
I honestly prefer the first printing of War from a functional standpoint.  The artwork is of inconsistent quality without a unified presentation, but I love the fact that I can bring the game anywhere in a box the size of a MtG Fatpack.  Devastation is a beautiful game and a lot of fun, but I hate lugging it around.  Storage is a hassle, and the best ways I've seen it organized involves pumping more money into modifying the box or outright ditching it for a new container.  I don't deal with that in War.  I love both games (and am happy to have hard copies) but I wish the storage could've been a bit more functional with Devastation.  I think BattleCON went a bit overboard with its stretch goals on that one.

I was first exposed to Devastation, however, so I mainly enjoy characters from that set.  My favorite in War is Zaamassal and I love playing with Joal and Shekhtur in Devastation.  I even got to have a lengthy chat in person with Zaamassal's creator a few months ago!

posts.name: cgrater
posts.cooked:
Foote:

It has very little haha

 

So really more of a demo/teaser for the analog game, then?

 

One of the things I like best about BCon is the strategic depth.  Similar to Chess/Go/Checkers, there is no element of luck.  Everything that happens in the game is a result of a player decision.  There is minimal hidden knowledge (the only thing hidden is what attack each opponent is playing right before revealing).  You always know exactly what cards your opponent has in hand and exactly what their capabilities are.

 

There is a really deep mind-game involved as well.  

Player 1: "I have this awesome attack"

Player 2: "I know you have that awesome attack, but I have this perfect counter"

Player 1: "Yes, but I have this different attack that could counter your counter"

Something of an "I know that you know that I know that you know…", but it really allows for a lot of strategic and tactical play, and even defeats are very satisfying.

 

Often, when I lose a competitive game, it is because of a bad dice roll, or a poor card flip (can even happen in Sentinels).  However, a loss in BattleCON is either because I made a mistake or because my opponent outplayed me.  Each defeat makes me a better player.

 

BattleCON cannot replace Sentinels, but in our house it has fired every other competitive game.  (BattleCON and Sentinels are the only two games we regularly keep in an easily accessible space in the living room.  All other games are in the closet in the back with the Hard Hat sign on the door).
